A field guide to fee estimation

Fees are a market. Every block has room for about four million weight units, and miners pick the transactions that pay the most per unit.

What wallets look at

  • The current mempool and how full it is.
  • How fast fees moved over the last few blocks.
  • How long the user is willing to wait.

Most wallets offer three choices. The fast option targets the next block, the normal option targets about an hour, and the slow option may take a day.

A worked example

PriorityRateCost
Fast25 sat/vB3,525 sats
Normal12 sat/vB1,692 sats

The same transaction of 141 virtual bytes costs more than twice as much when you are in a hurry. Waiting a little is often the cheapest choice.

Replacing a stuck transaction

  1. Check that the original transaction signals replace by fee.
  2. Create a new version that pays a higher rate.
  3. Broadcast the new version and wait for confirmation.

If the original did not signal replacement, the receiver can still speed it up by spending the unconfirmed output with a high fee. Miners then take both transactions together.

Fee estimation is never perfect. A good wallet explains its guess and lets you change it before you sign.

Over time the market settles into patterns. Weekends are often cheaper than weekdays, and quiet hours in one part of the world are busy in another.

Keeping an eye on these rhythms saves money without any special tools. A simple chart of recent blocks tells you most of what you need.
